A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VES research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including the new Appendix D in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic, GP-sample, and real-world optimization experiments, runtime measurements, and KS tests, including additional benchmark results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original optimization experiments and statistical tests, with revised performance plots, an additional evaluated baseline, and detailed KS p-value distributions.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the reported Gamma-shape update from solving Equation 13 directly to minimizing a squared residual plus an L2 penalty toward k = 1, with penalty weight 1. This modifies parameter selection within the retained VES framework. Algorithm 2 still references the unregularized equation.

E1.justification: The synthetic functions, GP-sample scenarios, and real-world tasks are unchanged. This includes Appendix B's Ackley, Michalewicz, Lasso-High, and Lasso-Hard benchmarks; no new dataset or task environment is introduced.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated UCB curves to Figures 4–7 alongside the retained EI/LogEI and MES comparisons. V1's stray VES-Gamma-Sequential references lack a distinct plotted curve, so their deletion does not establish removal of an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported inner-iteration limit from 50 to 5, also changing the runtime comparison's setting. Initialization, posterior sample count, BO evaluation horizons, metrics, and noiseless observation setting remain unchanged. This documents a revised budget without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: No new ablation, robustness test, or distinct diagnostic experiment is introduced. Figure 8 expands reporting of the existing KS comparison; Appendix D proposes acceleration without empirically evaluating it. Existing length-scale and numerical-equivalence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C expands statistical reporting from aggregate KS passing rates to per-benchmark distributions of p-values across 500 iterations in Figure 8. The ten repetitions, mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting, KS procedure, and 5% threshold remain unchanged; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Figures 4–7 substantially expand and revise the performance evidence through UCB results and updated VES-Gamma trajectories, including the GP curves and a Lasso-Hard trace now reaching 1000 iterations. Table 2 replaces 53.170 ± 15.433 seconds with 10.910 ± 12.323 seconds for VES under the changed iteration budget, not a same-setting speedup. Figure 8 adds detailed p-value results; Table 3's passing rates remain identical.

T1.justification: New Appendix D introduces a variable-projection value-function reformulation and gradient identity in Equations 18–19, using uniqueness of the inner optimum to motivate acceleration. The central lower-bound and EI-equivalence theorems and their Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the variational connection between EI and MES, VES-Gamma as a generalization, and competitive performance across low- and high-dimensional problems.

C2.justification: V2 newly attributes unregularized parameter instability tentatively to a flat optimization landscape and identifies LogEI as another possible explanation for empirical VES-Exp/EI discrepancies. Appendix D adds a specific acceleration prospect. Existing noise-related limitations and the tentative anti-EI interpretation remain.

D1.justification: V2 specifies Brent's method, the regularization weight, and the clamping target more explicitly. Section 4.1 replaces the promise of a future implementation release with a stated code repository link. These improve implementation and access documentation; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: V2 adds Jones et al. and Snoek et al. to the EI background, Brent for numerical minimization, and Golub–Pereyra and Poon–Peyré for variable projection. These are limited additions; the central positioning relative to EI, MES, and variational inference remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized explanatory additions, wording corrections, removal of stray VES-Gamma-Sequential mentions, publication information, acknowledgements, and Appendix D. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4–7 retain their panel organization but receive expanded legends and revised axes. V2 adds Figure 8's six p-value histograms and relocates several figures and Algorithm 2. The overall document layout and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves comparison breadth and transparency through UCB evaluations, detailed KS reporting, and clearer implementation and code-access information. The gains are limited by incomplete integration: Algorithm 2 still cites the unregularized update, and several captions omit UCB. The lower runtime uses a smaller iteration budget and does not establish a same-setting efficiency improvement.
